chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Abd Allah ibn al-Mughira, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a person in i'tikaf (seclusion in the mosque) who had intercourse with his wife, and he said: 'He is in the same position as one who broke his fast for a day during the month of Ramadan.'

key_terms.مُعْتَكِفٍ: A person performing i'tikaf, spiritual seclusion in a mosque

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a person in i'tikaf who has sexual intercourse with their spouse?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) equates the nullification of *i'tikaf* due to sexual intercourse with the penalty of breaking a single day of Ramadan's fast, highlighting the sanctity of the seclusion period. This ruling underscores the severity of intimate relations within the mosque precincts during *i'tikaf*, treating it as a significant breach of ritual purity and devotion comparable to a major fast-breaker. The comparison to Ramadan fasting reflects the high spiritual status accorded to *i'tikaf* in Shia jurisprudence, where it is viewed as a concentrated act of worship requiring strict adherence to boundaries.
